newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: PORTUGAL'S ALARDO WATER WITHDRAWN FROM MARKET.
newsitem.headline: PORTUGAL'S ALARDO WATER WITHDRAWN FROM MARKET.

text.p: Portuguese authorities have ordered a halt to the production and sale of Aguas do Alardo bottled water after it was found to contain plankton, a spokeswoman said on Wednesday.

"Authorities ordered a halt in production and sale of the water at the end of last week," said Maria Portugal, head of the environmental health division of the Directorate-General of Health, a department of the Health Ministry.
"It was found to contain plankton -- micro-organisms related to algae -- that could interfere with the public health and could cause gastro-intestinal problems," she told Reuters.

Aguas do Alardo, a unit of Belgian company Spadel which bottles water from northern Portugal, accounts for about 13 percent of the local bottled water market and is the second biggest Portuguese producer after Agua do Luso, newspapers said.

Portugal said the company was taking steps to eradicate the plankton and that the suspension of production would be lifted once health authorities had completed tests to show that the water was fit for consumption.
Local television showed images of supermarkets taking down Alardo bottled water from shelves.
